chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Personnel of the Majors and Minors band and Tuba Jack Jackson
summary: Willard reads the Majors and Minors names; Spikes identifies Bruce as a violinist used on banjo, and James Jackson as piano with Black and Tan and tuba in Johnny's band.

bands.name: Reb Spikes and His Majors and Minors Orchestra

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And the members of the Majors and Minors were George Bryant, Addison O'Neil, William Woodman, Eddie Morgan, Adam Mitchell, Fitz Weston, somebody Gordon on piano, and William Robinson, and somebody Bruce on banjo, George Morgan, Lawrence Craig and you, the leader. Is that right?
Yeah. Can't you see those other names?
No--well, in the McCarthy book, they're missing. Those names are missing. Uhh, do you...what was Gordon's first name?
Yeah. He was a violin player, too. Bruce played
lead violin with our show but on the jazz records, we would use him as a banjo, you see.

And...I just wanted to see if there was anybody else that we had not talked about. Oh, James...James Jackson, the one who wrote that "Teddy Bear," he was--was he the one that was known as "Tuba Jack"? That's what...it says here that there was someone named James "Tuba Jack" Jackson...

I think he did play tuba in the big band but he played piano in the...in the Black and Tan Orchestra. I think he played tuba but it's been so long... I think in the... You know, my big brother's ...my brother's big band--I think he played tuba in there if I'm not mistaken.
